headline: Pacific Jeans to shut oldest CEPZ unit due to safety risks
summary: The company is shutting down its 34-year-old factory to demolish structurally unsafe buildings and build a modern facility that could create 10,000 jobs.
details: Pacific Jeans Limited has begun shutting down operations at its oldest unit in the Chattogram Export Processing Zone (CEPZ), as the buildings were declared structurally unsafe by the RMG Sustainability Council (RSC).
The company has initiated a phased process to end the employment of approximately 5,000 workers at the facility, following the Bangladesh EPZ Labour Act, 2019.
The 34-year-old factory structure, consisting of three buildings, was the group's first facility at the CEPZ, established in 1994.

Managing Director Syed M Tanvir stated that the decision to suspend production was made to prioritize workers' lives and safety after a structural safety audit and Detailed Engineering Assessment (DEA) identified risks of failure.
Affected workers are being provided with maximum compensation, outstanding wages, overtime, unused earned leave, notice pay, and provident fund contributions.
The company is also providing workers with payslips, experience certificates, and letters of recommendation to assist their future employment prospects.
Pacific Jeans Group plans to construct a new, environment-friendly, state-of-the-art multi-storey factory at the same site after obtaining necessary approvals.
The new facility is expected to create around 10,000 jobs, and the company has stated that priority will be given to existing workers during recruitment for the new plant.

headline: S&P Global revises Meta’s outlook to ‘negative’
summary: The ratings agency cites significant uncertainty surrounding the social media giant's massive capital spending on AI investments.
details: S&P Global Ratings has revised its outlook on Meta Platforms to “negative” from “stable”. The agency cites significant uncertainty regarding the company's capital expenditure and free operating cash flow.

The AI boom has pushed capital expenditure across Big Tech to extreme levels. Meta forecast annual spending between $135 billion and $145 billion, following a free cash flow deficit of $2.12 billion in the third quarter.

To fund its AI buildout, Meta plans to sell $97.5 billion in stock. S&P Global warns that Meta's ability to monetize these AI investments is more limited than its peers, making it unclear when revenue will exceed rising costs.

S&P forecasts that Meta will generate free operating cash flow deficits of $39 billion in 2026 and $71 billion in 2027. The agency expects the company may need to fund its 2028 cash shortfall entirely with debt.
A Meta spokesperson told Reuters that the company disagrees with S&P's assertion about its AI monetization capabilities, stating that they see significant business opportunities ahead.
S&P Global also lowered the outlook on chipmaker Broadcom to 'stable' from 'positive' and previously lowered Oracle's credit rating to 'BBB-' due to heavy leverage.
